title: Minimum of a rotated list
prompt:
A list of distinct integers was sorted ascending and then rotated: some prefix was moved to the end (possibly none). Return the smallest value in O(log n) time.

- 1 to 100,000 distinct integers between -10^9 and 10^9.
hints: Compare the middle value with the last value. What does each outcome tell you about where the drop is?
If values[mid] > values[high], the minimum is strictly right of mid. Otherwise it is at mid or to its left.
Loop while low < high: low = mid + 1 in the first case, high = mid in the second. Return values[low].

solution.explanation: The rotated list is two ascending runs, and every value in the left run is larger than every value in the right run. Comparing values[mid] with values[high] reveals which run mid is in, so half the range can be discarded each step while keeping the minimum inside [low, high].

complexity.notes: Distinct values matter: with duplicates, values[mid] == values[high] gives no information and the worst case becomes O(n).

followUps: How does the algorithm change when duplicates are allowed?
